why: A single .. leaves the work-item directory while naming a file that exists, so a missing-file refusal cannot be what rejects it.
correct: Refuse: the resolved path is outside the work directory.

why: A deep climb to a file at the repository root.
correct: Refuse: containment is checked on the resolved path, not on depth.

why: The climb is hidden behind a descent, so a leading-.. check misses it.
correct: Refuse: normalise first, then check containment.

why: An absolute path is outside the work directory by definition.
correct: Refuse: absolute names are refused outright.

why: An absolute path that happens to resolve inside the directory still bypasses the name-under-directory contract.
correct: Refuse: the spec has the name resolved under the work-item directory, so an absolute name is refused.

why: An empty name resolves to the directory itself.
correct: Refuse: an empty name and the directory itself are not a cases file.

why: An in-directory entry that is a directory, not a regular file.
correct: Refuse: only a regular file is accepted.

why: A NUL byte can truncate the name at the filesystem call so a check sees a different path from the one opened.
correct: Refuse: a name with a NUL byte is a bad name.

why: A regular file directly in the work-item directory. Confinement must not refuse files that are inside it.
correct: Accept: a regular file in the directory is accepted by the confinement check.

why: A regular file one level down inside the directory. A rule that bans every / also bans legitimate subdirectories.
correct: Accept: a nested regular file that stays inside the directory is accepted.
